projects.name: Football Match & Betting-Market Model
bullets: Modelled 24,634 matches across 24 competitions with walk-forward backtesting, evaluated against closing market prices rather than short-run profit.
Priced same-match multiples with a joint simulation, using a correlation matrix estimated from historical residuals rather than multiplying leg odds.
Corrected for multiple comparisons across competitions: a league showing 9.4% ROI had a naive p of 0.032 but a family-wise p of 0.40, so it was reported as noise rather than edge.

projects.name: Customer Lifetime Value Prediction
bullets: Modelled 6-month customer spend from RFM behaviour on 1.07M real transactions using a leakage-safe temporal split.
XGBoost reached test R² 0.69 and MAE £600; the top 10% of predicted customers captured about 63% of actual future revenue against 10% at random.
Ranked the behavioural drivers of value with SHAP so the output was usable by marketing.

projects.name: Customer Churn Prediction
bullets: Predicted churn on 7,043 real telecom customers; logistic regression reached ROC-AUC 0.842 (5-fold CV 0.845) with 0.78 recall on the churn class.
Optimised for recall and ROC-AUC rather than accuracy, against a 73.5% majority baseline; the top 20% of predicted risk reaches about half of all churners.
Handled class imbalance and explained the drivers with coefficients and SHAP.

projects.name: Aviation Sentiment Classifier
bullets: Classified 14,640 real airline customer messages into three classes with custom scikit-learn transformers and a tuned pipeline.
Bag-of-words beat Word2Vec on short, irregular text; reported macro F1 rather than accuracy because the data skews heavily negative.
Deployed as a container image on AWS Lambda with CloudWatch monitoring, with preprocessing inside the fitted pipeline so serving cannot drift from training.

projects.name: Big Five Personality Analysis
bullets: Validated the five-factor structure on 603,000 real survey responses: within-trait item correlation 0.37 against 0.01 across traits, with a PCA elbow at exactly five.
Segmented respondents with K-Means but reported the clusters as weak, concluding that personality is dimensional rather than categorical.
